endorsements.quote: Regulatory bodies must work towards establishing clear guidelines for oversight, regulation, and accountability in AI diagnoses - holding the healthcare providers, users and AI developers responsible for their decisions and/or the healthcare systems that use these types of AI.
(ii) Voluntary participation - the option to opt out of remote monitoring without facing any negative consequences or reduced quality of care ( 67 );

A key issue was that patients/participants should be fully informed about the nature of the remote monitoring technology and their diagnosis accuracy, often lower than traditional “in-person” oral health assessments ( 22 ).

To overcome the digital divide, there is a need to promote a digitally inclusive society through internet commuter technologies and strategies that increase access to internet connectivity and technology, strengthen digital awareness, and improve digital literacy in oral health through training to reduce disparities and inequalities.

Ensuring the security of EHRs is crucial to prevent data breaches, cyberattacks, and unauthorized access, and it is an ethical responsibility of the provider/organization to implement robust security measures, ensure encryption protocols are in place, and have access controls in place that protect patients' data from these threats ( 36 ).

unlisted_practices: Validate AI diagnostic systems and continuously monitor their performance before and during clinical use.
Preserve patients' right to seek a second opinion from a human provider rather than relying solely on an AI-generated diagnosis.
Maintain human oversight of AI diagnoses so AI does not replace human clinical judgment.
Address bias in AI diagnoses to ensure fairness and non-discrimination.
Establish legal frameworks clarifying liability and stakeholder roles when AI-driven diagnoses harm patients.
Train patients to use remote monitoring devices correctly and make them aware of emergency-assistance limitations.
Use a multidisciplinary approach involving clinicians, AI developers, and policymakers to address AI ethical issues.
Retain a copy of the intraoral device design blueprint in patient records and require dentist approval before refabrication.
